system.summary: Letter substitution with a few homophones and several signs that stand for two to four letters as transcribed (look-alike shapes not yet split), word signs (je, le, que, la, pour) and name codes (la Rochelle, Monsieur du Mayne), and nulls including a divider stroke. Tomokiyo's 'St. Luc's Cipher' table, corrected by Brackx.
system.doubled_letters: Separate signs for rr, ll, ss and mm.
system.sibling_key: Same table as St. Luc's f. 245r-v (with contemporary margin decipherments). Not the cipher of f. 43 (saintluc1586, George Lasry's key), which is another table.
system.notes: Labels are Brackx's (brackx2026/label_legend.md). Multi-valued labels (z = u/v/h/m, 9 and 9q = n/m/g, S = m/s/g/mm, f = c/s, p = i/r, 6 = s/y, y = n/d, d = l/c/p, t/tb = p/t/v/r, pi = f/s) carry 40.5% of the letters on f. 260r and 34.5% on f. 260v; they are most likely look-alike shapes merged in transcription, not designed polyphony, but that is not yet shown on the image.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana henryiii page, 'St. Luc's Cipher': the key table and the opening line of f. 260 ('arriva hier en Olleron ... sans retourner a'); f. 260 otherwise called undeciphered. No other reading found (Brackx, web search; this repository).

conditions.human_role: Michael Brackx, working with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), transcribed f. 245r-v and f. 260r-v sign by sign, corrected Tomokiyo's table on the f. 245 margin decipherments, decoded f. 260 with a beam search under a French model and built a reading line by line with English (issue #90). In this repository: measurement against the read bar, the look-alike grading, the target record and write-up.
tools: Brackx's align.py, cover.py and crib scorer (not in the repository)

solution.what: Tomokiyo's 'St. Luc's Cipher' table (cryptiana henryiii) encoded as labels with values; nulls and the word signs kept (Brackx, #90).
f. 245r-v (cipher passages, 423 signs) and f. 260r-v (26 and 29 lines, 2,428 tokens) transcribed sign by sign from deskewed full-size line crops (Brackx with Claude Code, #90).

The margin decipherments of f. 245v (crib 1) and f. 245r (crib 2) aligned with their cipher: key corrections Δo = Monsieur du Mayne, ʞ = pour, ⊔ = la Rochelle, new signs ss and la, Ↄ = rr, crossed ʒ = h, plain 3 = m, ♀/♁ = n/p, x; letter agreement 89.3% (f. 245v) and 83.2% (f. 245r) under the corrected Essais model, shuffled-key controls 11-31%.

f. 260r-v decoded by beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram; 741 single-value key candidates tried; corpus-word coverage 79.2% / 80.7% (controls 27-46% / 31-49%). A decoder bug that skipped lines beginning with the label # was fixed (r. 8, v. 19 restored).

Brackx's reading of f. 260r-v in the writer's spelling with every unread run sized and an English translation (#90, reply of 23 Oct 2026): Oléron, the shallops and galliots, the stone-laden ships against the palisade, the unpaid garrison, the Rochelais passports and the salt of the grand parti. 22 letters read with another value of the same label than the decoder chose.

Read bar applied (v10_relabel.measure): f. 260r 0.761 and f. 260v 0.851 of words read as sense. Letters on multi-valued labels are 40.5% / 34.5% of the text, over the 3% look-alike limit, so both pages are graded decoded, not read whatever their share; the readings are kept as partial readings with English.

Method restored: key obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's published table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments, decodes f. 260r-v into French that largely builds sentences (0.761 / 0.851 of words), but 40.5% / 34.5% of the letters fall on labels with several values chosen by a language model, so the text is decoded, not read. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 24 Oct 2026: texts/reading_f260r.md 0.761 and reading_f260v.md 0.851 of words read as sense (v10), but both decoded, not read under the look-alike limit, so nothing counts as read.

texts.label: f. 260r
texts.summary: St. Luc to Henri III from Brouage, June 1586: a Rochelais commander has come to Oléron and watched his galliots attack the Brouage shallops; the Rochelais try to block the harbour with ships loaded with stone, one of six score tons, and the garrison has taken one of them.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 76.1% of the words of texts/reading_f260r.md read as sense (v10), and 40.5% of the letters fall on multi-valued labels (3% look-alike limit): decoded, not read. Brackx's reading is kept as a partial reading.

texts.label: f. 260v
texts.summary: The garrison is unpaid and losing hope, with no word of the King's commands since April; La Rochelle means to keep the sea and sell passports to its captains; St. Luc protests that the council has let the tax-farmers of the grand parti buy salt at La Rochelle and asks that French merchants be forbidden to take salt there on pain of confiscation.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 85.1% of the words of texts/reading_f260v.md read as sense (v10), and 34.5% of the letters fall on multi-valued labels (3% look-alike limit): decoded, not read. Brackx's reading is kept as a partial reading.
